<reason>A wins a clear but competitive debate. B persuasively explained why headlines influence policy, but A better defended the actual alternative: growth as a constrained economic benchmark, alongside explicit social obligations. A answered both pressure questions directly and challenged B’s repeated assumption that GDP primacy excludes other policy reasons. B’s life-satisfaction proposal substantially clarified measurement, but its handling of distributional conflicts and future benefits did not establish superior accountability over A’s arrangement.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s distinction between “primary” and “exclusive” undercut B’s hidden-zero argument. Binding social protections can defeat a GDP-raising policy while growth remains the main economic target. B repeatedly asserted that governments could reason only in the headline’s currency rather than squarely defeating this comparison.</best_rebuttal>
